newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW-Juppe French election platform speech.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Juppe French election platform speech.

text.p: Following are comments from economists on Prime Minister Alain Juppe speech on centre-right coalition's platform for May/June parliamentary election.

Juppe called for more tax cuts, reduced company charges, reform of state's role in economy via privatisations, said unemployment was still the government's "obsession" and said he ruled out a shift to "hyperliberalism".
JEAN-LOUIS MOURIER, ECONOMIST, LOUIS DREYFUS FINANCE
"I think this follows the line set by Chirac. It's not a change in (economic) policy, but more a referendum on current policy, perhaps with a little acceleration on spending cuts."
"The ultraliberal option pushed by some...has been rejected"
PHILIPPE BROSSARD, SENIOR ECONOMIST, ABN AMRO
The two main axes for this campaign will be lower taxes, which as far as the government is concerned means lower spending and, point two, Europe.
The result (of the election) is going to be very, very close to call. The big question mark will be over future opinion polls.
ANTOINE BRUNET, ECONOMIST, CREDIT COMMERCIAL DE FRANCE
Basically it fits the lines mapped out by Chirac, with a degree of twist towards greater liberalism while avoiding the word...due to the reticence of the electorate on this term.
There' a bit more liberalism but maintenance of the social welfare structure.
The markets know the stakes. If the RPR/UDF (party) coalition returns there will be more reform than in the reverse case. What will move the markets is the opinion polls.
